_readme: THE NON-HUMAN LINEAR IDENTITIES (DRE-3172). One file, read by the check —
and, since DRE-3321, by scripts/linear_ops.py for the set of names a run
may declare in LINEAR_IDENTITY when it says whose budget it just spent.
Since 2026-09-05 the workspace has three Linear users, and two of them are
not people. The FLEET user is the one every sweep, planner, merge-sync,
relay and console run as. The OPERATOR-TOOLS user is the one the
operator's scripts and assistant sessions run as. The third is the CEO,
who approves, and is the only admin among them.
WHY TWO. Linear's 2,500 requests/hour limit is PER USER. Two non-human
users are two separate budgets, so a heavy read from the operator's
terminal no longer starves every sweep in the fleet (and the other way
round). That is the whole point, and it is the thing that silently stops
being true in two ways nobody would notice: a key rotated onto an admin's
user, or both keys resolving to the SAME user — one budget again, with
nothing on the board looking any different.
So each identity is declared here with the rules it owes, and
`python3 scripts/check_linear_identities.py check` asks Linear
`viewer { id name admin }` for each key and fails, naming the rule, when
the declaration and the truth disagree. A key that is absent is reported
UNKNOWN and the check exits non-zero: unknown is never a pass.
TWO PLACES A KEY LIVES, AND THE NAME COLLIDES. `env` is the variable THE
CHECK reads the key from, and the check is written for the operator's
machine: there `LINEAR_API_KEY` is the operator-tools key (from .env) and
the fleet key must be handed over separately as `LINEAR_API_KEY_FLEET`.
In GitHub Actions the same name `LINEAR_API_KEY` is the FLEET key — every
workflow reads `secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY`. `lives_in` says where each key
is actually kept. A reader who conflates the two will misfile a key.
WHY A HOME (DRE-3334). One identity's key is not kept in one place, and
each copy can rot on its own. `homes` declares the extra ones: a short
`name` unique within the identity, the `env` the check reads that copy
from (unique across this whole file), and `lives_in`. The top-level `env`
and `lives_in` ARE the identity's first home. The fleet's second home is
the relay Lambda's key: until agent-bureau PR #2299 the relay's deploy
copied the operator's `LINEAR_API_KEY` into it on every deploy, and that
variable has been the bureau-tools key since 2026-09-05 — one routine
deploy would have put every parking reason, escalation and receipt the
relay writes on the operator's user and the operator's budget, with
nothing on the board looking any different. The deploy guard that stops
that lives in the other repo; this check outlives any deploy script, so
after a relay deploy one command with the relay's key exported says whose
budget the relay is on. `one_user_per_identity` is the rule it owes:
every home of an identity must be the same user as its first home.
No user ids here on purpose: an id pinned in a file is the thing that
goes stale on the next rotation. The display name is the declared fact;
the check prints the id it resolved so the operator can record it.
JSON, not YAML, like its siblings: the reader must import with no pip
install. Check this file and the live keys:
python3 scripts/check_linear_identities.py check

identities.name: fleet
identities.lives_in: GitHub Actions secret LINEAR_API_KEY in every product repo (read by every workflow as secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY), and the operator's own copy of it in .env as LINEAR_API_KEY_FLEET
identities.purpose: The user every unattended actor writes to Linear as: the sweeps, the planner, merge-sync, the relay and the console.

homes.name: relay
homes.lives_in: AWS Secrets Manager bureau/relay/linear-api-key — the relay Lambda's own key in agent-bureau, exported by the operator into LINEAR_API_KEY_RELAY before this check runs

identities.name: operator-tools
identities.lives_in: The operator's .env as LINEAR_API_KEY, and AWS Secrets Manager bureau/operator-tools/linear-api-key
identities.purpose: The user the operator's own scripts and assistant sessions read and write Linear as, on a budget the fleet cannot spend.
